subtopic: Converting Monthly Fees to Annual Percentage Costs
source_evidence: A $3 monthly subscription-based fee could result in an annual advisory fee totaling $36. That’s more than 7% of the account’s value.
answer: To express a monthly subscription fee as an annual percentage of an account, first multiply the monthly fee by 12 to get the yearly cost. Then divide that cost by the account balance and multiply by 100. For example, a $3 monthly fee costs $36 per year. On a $500 account, that is 7.2% of the account’s value for the year.
